conventions.convention: Reflection length uses all conjugates T of simple reflections, includes the empty product, and u ≤T v means ℓT(v)=ℓT(u)+ℓT(u⁻¹v). M(A)=im(A−id), F(A)=ker(A−id).
The Wall form uses (A−id)⁻¹, giving symmetric part −B/2. Orthogonal subspace restrictions need not belong to the Coxeter group.
Moved-space inclusion implies absolute-order comparison only for elements below a common upper bound.

Simple roots have B-norm one. The two commuting color classes are ordered J then K; c=ab. Prefix roots and dual vectors start at index 1, with cyclic simple-root and dual-vector indices modulo n. μ(v)=−2(CV−id)⁻¹v is initially conditional on invertibility.
The nh/2 positive-root count is for irreducible finite type; reducible systems use component counts and componentwise operators. Rank one and the empty system are separated explicitly.
For roots ai<aj, compatibility is R(aj)R(ai) ≤T c. X(c) is the resulting clique complex; X(σ) is full on Pσ. Prefixes are inclusive. The empty face has cone {0} and empty spherical realization.

The noncrossing definition extends reflection-length formulas to possibly infinite groups, but the lattice and complement theorems assume finite type. Reducible intervals are componentwise products; the empty product is a singleton. K(w)=w⁻¹c.

Type-A permutations compose right to left; fixed points count as cycles. Noncrossing means disjoint convex hulls of distinct blocks. The classical complement uses white di after black bi, so K² rotates labels by i↦i−1.
The bipartite A3 examples use B(x,y)=½Σxiyi, making Ei−Ej unit roots; the batch-18 permutation examples instead use (Ei−Ej)/√2 with the standard Euclidean inner product.

load_bearing.statement: For a finite-type Coxeter system, ℓT(w)=dim M(w)=dim V−dim F(w). Absolute order is a graded partial order with shortest-reflection-prefix description. If α,β ≤T δ, then α ≤T β iff M(α)⊆M(β); in particular equal moved spaces force α=β.

For orthogonal A on a finite-dimensional real inner-product space, M(A)=F(A)⊥. Every subspace U⊆M(A) has a unique restriction AU below A with M(AU)=U; U↦AU is an order isomorphism onto {B:B ≤O A}. The Wall form restricts accordingly. Orthogonal reflection length equals moved dimension.

For finite-type W and w≠1, there is a root α with F(w)⊆Hα; every such α lies in M(w), and dim M(w)=1+dim M(tαw). Every w factors into exactly dim M(w) reflections. When dim M(t1⋯tm)=m, the prefix-conjugated root normals are independent and span that moved space.

For irreducible finite type of rank n≥2, the bipartite element c of order h has Coxeter-plane rotation 2π/h; root-hyperplane traces are exactly h reflection lines. The first nh/2 prefix roots are precisely Φ+, the next nh/2 are Φ−, all nh are distinct, and CV−id is invertible with μ(ρi)=μi. Rank one and reducible systems are treated separately.

For the stated irreducible finite-type bipartite data of rank n≥2, μi·ρi=1, μi spans F(R(ρi)c), μi·ρj≥0 for i≤j in the positive-root range, and μj·ρi≤0 for i<j. For σ ≤T c, Pσ is the positive-root set of Wσ={w:M(w)⊆M(σ)}, with the canonical simple system and increasing reduced tuple θ specified in clause (4). Every eligible increasing rank-k tuple in Pσ dominates θ componentwise.

For an increasing positive-root tuple a1<⋯<ak, ℓT(R(a1)⋯R(ak)c)=n−k iff μ(ai)·aj=0 for every i>j. Its set is a face iff its reverse product lies below c with reflection length k. Face roots are independent; X(σ) has dimension ℓT(σ)−1; and c[F]∩c[F′]=c[F∩F′].

For σ ≤T c, σ≠1, and eligible prefixes τi≥θk, c[X(σ,τi)]=Y(σ,τi)=Z(σ,τi), a full-dimensional closed convex cone in M(σ). At the endpoint, c[X(σ)]=c[Pσ]=M(σ)∩⋂j μ(θj)+. Its sphere section is spherically convex, and |X(α)∩X(β)|=|X(α)|∩|X(β)| for α,β ≤T c.

For subcomplexes Y,Z of the finite bipartite root complex, c[Y∩Z]=c[Y]∩c[Z] and |Y∩Z|=|Y|∩|Z|. If their intersection has a vertex and its cone C is convex, every maximal common simplex F satisfies span(F)=span(C). No identification with the intersection of the two ambient spans is asserted.

For independent unit vectors σ1,…,σk in a finite-dimensional real inner-product space, M(R(σk)⋯R(σ1))=span(σ1,…,σk), of dimension k, including k=0. For root normals in finite type, the corresponding group product has reflection length k.

Every finite-type noncrossing interval [1,c] is a finite lattice, componentwise for reducible systems. In the bipartite connected case, a maximal common root-complex face constructs a∧b, with M(a∧b)=span(|X(a)|∩|X(b)|) and P(a∧b)=Pa∩Pb. Conjugation between Coxeter elements gives lattice isomorphisms.

For finite type, K(w)=w⁻¹c is a lattice anti-automorphism of [1,c], K²(w)=c⁻¹wc, and ℓT(K(w))=|S|−ℓT(w). In type A on N≥1 labels, ℓT(w)=N−cycle_count(w), and w ≤T (1⋯N) iff its cycle-support partition is noncrossing and every cycle is cyclically increasing. The support map is a poset isomorphism and identifies K with the classical interleaved complement.
